**Automated red teaming is a search for failures, and the evaluator can itself be wrong.** A generator proposes diverse tests against an authorized isolated system; a judge identifies candidate failures; reviewers verify whether the observed behavior actually violated the intended requirement. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08073) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.05566)

Optimizing only an attack-success score can cause the generator to repeat one pattern or exploit weaknesses in the judge. Include coverage and diversity, and preserve examples with their model, tool, and environment versions.

**Separate discovery from final evaluation.** If defenses are repeatedly tuned on the same prompts, success on those prompts may reflect memorization. Maintain independent tests and regression cases for previously verified failures.

Measure severity, reproducibility, false positives, and impact on benign tasks. Findings should lead to concrete changes such as tool restrictions, validation, or better handling of untrusted content, followed by retesting. A dashboard of adversarial prompts is not an improved system until verified failures have been addressed. Keep tools and data controlled so testing cannot affect unrelated users or external systems.

**Technical details and references.**

Automated red teaming can generate diverse test prompts and score failures, but the exercise should target an authorized isolated system with controlled tools and data. Optimize both discovered failure severity and coverage/diversity so the generator does not repeat a single exploit pattern. Use human adjudication to separate actual failures from evaluator errors. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08073) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.05566)

Partition test discovery from final evaluation to avoid overfitting defenses to the same prompts. Maintain a reproducible corpus, versioned model/tool configurations, and regression checks for repaired cases. Measure false positives and benign-task utility alongside attack success. Reward-model scores are proxies, not proof of safety; adversarially optimizing them can expose weaknesses in the judge instead of the system. Feed verified findings into concrete controls and retest.
